title: Direct summands of perfect complexes over a ring are perfect
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $K,L$ be objects of the derived category $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If $K\oplus L$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], then both $K$ and $L$ are perfect.

proof.text: Unpack IsPerfectRingComplex of S = K biprod L as a finite-projective complex P with strict bounds a,b and an isomorphism S to Q(P). Apply exists_finiteFree_model_of_finite_projective to P and upper bound b. Its quasi-isomorphism f becomes an isomorphism under Q; composing with the model isomorphism exhibits IsPseudoCoherent S. Apply the already stated and proved pseudoCoherent_summand directly to the derived objects K and L. No choice of separate complex representatives is needed.

Each term P.X i is flat by Module.Flat.of_projective; translate this to categorical flatness with ModuleCat.flat_iff_flat. Apply the existing proved source lemma torAmplitudeIn_Q_obj_of_flat, recorded by lem-trf-source-bounded-flat-tor-amplitude. Transport its Tor amplitude across S isomorphic to Q(P). Widen the lower endpoint to min a b to ensure the ordered interval required by the final perfectness criterion, including the case a>b. The generic source theorem already packages the K-flat computation, so the separate bounded-module K-flatness theorem and mixed-coefficient derived tensor existence theorem are unnecessary.

Construct Retract K S from biprod.inl, biprod.fst and biprod.inl_fst, and Retract L S from biprod.inr, biprod.snd and biprod.inr_snd. The existing IsStableUnderRetracts instance for torAmplitudeIn transfers the common interval [min a b,b] to each summand. It maps the retract through tensoring with each degree-zero test module and uses stability of homologyConcentratedIn under retracts, exactly the Tag 066G argument.

For each summand T apply isPerfect_of_pseudoCoherent_finiteTorAmplitude with its pseudo-coherence and the ordered interval [min a b,b]. Unpack the resulting complex E, bounds c,d, finite generation, projectivity and isomorphism Q(E) to T. Convert the termwise support conditions to E.IsStrictlyGE c and E.IsStrictlyLE d using the Mathlib equivalences. Reverse the model isomorphism to obtain exactly IsPerfectRingComplex T. Pair the conclusions for K and L.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q116-6484b5030 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full, the statement of each of the 9 nodes it cites, and the Stacks text of more-algebra.tex at 066S, 0658, 064X, 066G and the tor-amplitude definition. The item statement matches 066S exactly: A is a commutative ring, the objects are in D(A), and perfect means a bounded complex of finitely generated projective modules. The six steps follow the source route of 0658, 064X and 066G. Step 1: the free-model lemma from 064U gives pseudo-coherence. Step 2: the last clause of the ring pseudo-coherence summand lemma (064X). Step 3: projective implies flat (a Mathlib leaf), and a bounded-above flat complex is K-flat (064K). Step 4: the K-flat clause (2) of the derived tensor functor gives one Tor interval [a,b] for every module M. Step 5: the 066G retract argument written out; it is genuinely elementary. Step 6: the ring criterion from 0658, applied to K and to L separately. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and there is no cycle. There are no new nodes. The only similar existing nodes (lem-pc-perfect-summand and the thick-closure lemma) are about D(O_X) on a scheme, a different object, so there is no duplicate. I accept the five declared off-unit tool uses; each is a generic algebra lemma that no node of sk-thm-sf-package states. Edge cases checked: A=0, a zero summand, and a projective but non-free summand over a non-Noetherian ring. Two defects in existing nodes need maintenance; neither is in this delivery, so they do not block it. First, lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-finite-tor-perfect links D(R) and 'perfect' to the scheme definitions, although its text and conclusion are explicitly about the ring. Second, lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-summand cites 064T where the tag is 064U. No fixes were written.
